articles.headline: Delhi August rain already in excess with three weeks to go
articles.summary: Delhi has recorded 234.5mm of rain in the first 10 days of August, surpassing the monthly long-period average of 233.1mm. This is the earliest the city has reached this mark in at least 15 years. The heavy showers have helped keep temperatures below normal, with more rain predicted over the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Man allegedly kills two daughters and attempts suicide at Bengaluru hotel
articles.summary: A 35-year-old man allegedly murdered his daughters, aged five and 10, before attempting suicide at a luxury hotel near Bengaluru's international airport. Police found a suicide note citing an argument with his wife as the reason. The suspect is currently being treated at a hospital while under police custody.

articles.headline: SC orders FIRs for all missing people, warns states of contempt
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has directed all states and Union territories to immediately register FIRs whenever a person is reported missing, regardless of age or gender. The bench warned that failure to comply with this order would lead to contempt proceedings against chief secretaries and police chiefs.

articles.headline: Firing at disputed Arunachal-Assam border injures 12 people
articles.summary: At least 12 people from Assam were injured after unidentified gunmen opened fire along the disputed interstate border with Arunachal Pradesh. The incident occurred in the Mingmang Badati area. Police are investigating the clash, which is linked to a long-standing boundary dispute over an 800 km stretch.

articles.headline: 18 candidates shortlisted for first CEO of Ram Temple Trust
articles.summary: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has shortlisted 18 candidates for the position of its first chief executive officer. A three-member panel will conduct interviews in Ayodhya to select a candidate from over 5,200 applicants. The new CEO will manage the temple's administration and facilities.

articles.headline: Samudra Manthan scheme aims to boost India's offshore petroleum production
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet has approved the Samudra Manthan scheme with a ₹54,084 crore outlay to enhance India's petroleum production. The scheme focuses on seismic data acquisition and processing to unlock vast offshore potential, aiming to reduce the country's high dependence on crude oil imports.

articles.headline: Students and police clash in Ranchi over Jharkhand recruitment irregularities
articles.summary: Thousands of students protesting alleged irregularities in state recruitment exams clashed with police in Ranchi. Security forces used water cannons and tear gas to stop demonstrators marching toward the state assembly. The protest stems from concerns over the Jharkhand Public Service Commission's exam process.

articles.headline: Courts must not allow attire to be used to blame women: HC
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has stated that a woman's choice of clothing should not be used as a justification for unlawful conduct or to diminish her dignity. The court emphasized that the focus of legal proceedings must remain on the conduct of the accused rather than the attire of the victim.

articles.headline: Luxury hotels and eateries in Bengaluru raided over food safety concerns
articles.summary: Food safety officials raided 60 luxury hotels and eateries in Bengaluru, uncovering issues such as rotten meat, expired products, and the use of unapproved additives. Several establishments were served notices, and significant quantities of substandard food items were seized and destroyed during the drive.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM guarantees water security as seventh state promise
articles.summary: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has announced that water security will be the Karnataka government's seventh guarantee. The initiative aims to recharge groundwater, fill lakes, and ensure that water reaches farmers across the state. The CM emphasized the completion of irrigation projects to achieve this goal.

articles.headline: Karnataka statewide bandh on August 13 to proceed as planned
articles.summary: Pro-Kannada activists have confirmed that a statewide bandh will take place on August 13 to protest against the release of Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. Despite some divisions among activist groups, the organizers have called for a total shutdown of services to express their dissent over the water sharing issue.

articles.headline: 39 people arrested with ₹55 crore worth of drugs in Bengaluru
articles.summary: In a major multi-state operation, Bengaluru police arrested 39 people and seized narcotics worth approximately ₹55.80 crore. The contraband included MDMA, cocaine, and ganja. The operation targeted drug peddling networks operating across 10 states and involving several foreign nationals.

articles.headline: Savarkar quiz row: BJP accuses IUML of misusing power in Kerala
articles.summary: The BJP has accused the IUML of misusing its influence in the Kerala government after a school teacher was suspended for including a question about V.D. Savarkar in a 'freedom quiz'. The teacher was suspended following protests from the IUML's student wing, leading to a political face-off over historical figures.

articles.headline: Four medical students suspended for ragging after junior doctor's death
articles.summary: Authorities at a Gujarat medical college have suspended four second-year students for six months for their involvement in ragging. The move follows the death of a first-year resident doctor who was found dead in his hostel room. An internal inquiry found evidence of mental harassment and physical abuse.

articles.headline: Amritpal's party fields Indira Gandhi assassin's son for Punjab polls
articles.summary: The party of jailed MP Amritpal Singh has announced that Sarabjit Singh Khalsa, the son of Indira Gandhi's assassin Beant Singh, will contest the upcoming Punjab assembly elections. He will run from the Bhadaur constituency as an independent candidate supported by the radical Panthic group.

articles.headline: Trump demands Iran pay compensation for deaths from past attacks
articles.summary: U.S. Presidential candidate Donald Trump has demanded that Iran pay compensation for American lives lost in past regional conflicts. His statements come amid heightened tensions in the Middle East and ongoing rhetoric regarding Iran's support for proxy groups and its nuclear program.

articles.headline: India condemns defacing of its embassy in Slovenia with graffiti
articles.summary: The Indian government has strongly condemned the defacing of its embassy in Slovenia with anti-India and pro-Khalistan graffiti. New Delhi has taken up the matter with Slovenian authorities, seeking an investigation and the arrest of those responsible for the act of vandalism against the diplomatic mission.

articles.headline: Oceans hit record-high temperatures in July, climate reports show
articles.summary: Global sea surface temperatures reached record highs in July 2026, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service. Scientists warn that the warming oceans are contributing to more extreme weather events and could disrupt marine ecosystems, with temperatures remaining significantly above historical averages.

articles.headline: India seeks new bowling identity without injured Jasprit Bumrah
articles.summary: As India prepares for the Test series against Sri Lanka without the injured Jasprit Bumrah, the team is looking to redefine its bowling strategy. Senior players like Mohammed Siraj will need to lead a relatively inexperienced pace attack, while the team explores more flexibility among its spinners.

articles.headline: PM Modi lauds athletes' efforts at Glasgow Commonwealth Games celebrations
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a reception for India's athletes who participated in the Glasgow Commonwealth Games. He praised their performance, particularly those from rural backgrounds and the armed forces, noting that their success continues to inspire the nation and elevate India's standing in global sports.

articles.headline: Meta launches Muse Glimmer AI for Macs and PCs
articles.summary: Meta has launched Muse Glimmer, an AI tool designed to run complex tasks on Macs or PCs using graphics cards without cloud computing. Mark Zuckerberg stated the open-weight models aim to strengthen US competition with China in the AI sector by allowing developers to run powerful models locally.

articles.headline: Opposition continues protest as government offers statement from Amit Shah
articles.summary: Parliamentary proceedings were disrupted as the opposition demanded a statement from PM Modi on the embezzlement of Ram temple funds. While the government offered a statement from Home Minister Amit Shah, the opposition remained firm on their demand, leading to several adjournments in both houses.

articles.headline: Karnataka to launch one-year menopause fellowship for medical professionals
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is planning to introduce a first-of-its-kind one-year fellowship in menopause for postgraduate doctors. The program, offered through RGUHS, aims to create a specialist workforce to manage peri-menopause and menopause care within the public health system.

articles.headline: Gurgaon DLF penthouse sells for record 27 crore rupees
articles.summary: An entrepreneur has purchased a luxury penthouse at DLF's The Dahlias in Gurgaon for 27 crore rupees. The deal rivals major Mumbai transactions on a per-square-foot basis, marking Gurgaon's emergence as a top luxury real estate powerhouse in India with prices crossing Rs 2 lakh per sq ft.

articles.headline: Metro double-decker project in Bengaluru likely to be shortened significantly
articles.summary: The BMRCL is considering reducing the proposed 37km double-decker flyover-cum-metro stretch to just 11km due to engineering challenges and high costs. The original plan aimed to connect Hebbal to Silk Board, but the revised plan focuses on major junctions to ease traffic congestion.

articles.headline: Voter list in Karnataka shrinks by three lakh in six days
articles.summary: Nearly 3 lakh voters were removed from the electoral rolls in Karnataka between August 3 and 9 during a special revision drive. Bengaluru accounted for the largest reduction. The Election Commission stated the deletions were due to voters being absent, shifted, or having duplicate entries.

articles.headline: Fraudster posing as IAS officer held in Patna with luxury assets
articles.summary: Patna police arrested a man for posing as an IAS officer and operating a fraudulent investment firm. The accused possessed a Tesla car, a luxury bungalow with a swimming pool, and 29 firearms. He allegedly claimed to be an advisor to the National Security Advisor to deceive high-profile victims.

articles.headline: Government hints at JPC for FCRA Bill amid opposition rollback demand
articles.summary: The Union government has indicated it may refer the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) following intense opposition. Opposition parties have demanded a total rollback of the bill, claiming it unfairly targets minority groups and NGOs.

articles.headline: Oil product exports find new markets in Spain and Italy
articles.summary: Due to the West Asia crisis, Indian oil product exports have surged in new markets including Spain, Italy, and Singapore. Exports to Spain grew by 15% in the last quarter, while shipments to Tanzania and Sri Lanka also saw significant increases as Indian refineries diversified their global reach.

articles.headline: Sarfaraz Khan returns to Indian squad for Sri Lanka Test series
articles.summary: Batsman Sarfaraz Khan has been recalled to the Indian Test squad for the upcoming series against Sri Lanka. This follows his impressive performance in the Ranji Trophy and his previous stint with the national team. His inclusion is seen as a move to bolster the middle-order batting lineup.

articles.headline: Deepanshu suspended for doping violation, to miss Asian Games
articles.summary: Indian Greco-Roman wrestler Deepanshu has been provisionally suspended by the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) after testing positive for a prohibited anabolic steroid. The suspension rules him out of the upcoming Asian Games and could lead to a long-term ban from the sport.

articles.headline: India begins FIH Hockey World Cup campaign against Wales on August 15
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team is set to open its FIH Hockey World Cup campaign against Wales on Independence Day. Led by Harmanpreet Singh, the team has undergone rigorous training, including a boot camp in the Swiss Alps, to prepare for the tournament and aim for a podium finish.

articles.headline: Scientists discover active undersea 'river' of sediment in Arabian Sea
articles.summary: Researchers have mapped a 733km-long active underwater channel system in the Arabian Sea that functions like a river. This "river" transports organic carbon and nutrients to the deep sea, potentially holding significant oil and gas reservoirs. It is the second-largest mapped channel system in the world.

articles.headline: Eight countries participate in immersive Jainism study program in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Nearly three dozen scholars from eight countries gathered in Ladnun, Rajasthan, for an immersive summer program to study Jain texts and philosophy. The program involved living alongside monks and nuns to experience Jain practices, meditation, and the community's lifestyle firsthand over several weeks.

articles.headline: India plans over 50,000 crore investment for green energy corridor
articles.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is seeking Cabinet approval for the ₹50,000-crore third phase of the Green Energy Corridor. The scheme aims to strengthen intra-state transmission networks in renewable-rich states like Gujarat and Rajasthan to reduce generation curtailment. Currently, inadequate infrastructure causes electricity curtailment equivalent to 18% of monthly solar output.

articles.headline: Adani Infra (India) Ltd emerges as major cash generator for conglomerate
articles.summary: Adani Infra (India) Ltd (AIIL) reported a profit of ₹7,127 crore in FY26, showing 13-fold revenue growth over two years. Designated as the project management and EPC arm for the Adani Group, it generated ₹6,666 crore in free cash flow. AIIL is utilizing these profits to acquire significant minority stakes in four listed group companies, including Adani Green and Adani Energy Solutions.

articles.headline: Vodafone Idea reports first quarterly subscriber addition since 2018 merger
articles.summary: Vodafone Idea Ltd added subscribers for the first time since its 2018 merger, with its customer base rising to 193.1 million in Q1. The company narrowed its net loss to ₹3,754 crore, significantly beating market estimates. Growth was driven by network expansion and higher data consumption. The telco is currently in talks to raise ₹35,000 crore in bank debt to fund 4G and 5G rollouts.

articles.headline: Indian sweet makers grapple with rising dairy costs before festive season
articles.summary: Confectioners like Bikaji and Sweet Bengal are facing increased production costs as prices for milk, ghee, and butter rise by 10-30%. While some brands plan price hikes of up to 10% for Diwali, others are absorbing costs to maintain festive sales volumes. The pressure is particularly high for milk-based Bengali sweets, as the industry competes for limited milk fat supplies.

articles.headline: BSNL proposes 77,000 crore investment for 4G and 5G network expansion
articles.summary: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd (BSNL) has proposed a ₹77,000-crore capital expenditure plan over five years. The strategy includes setting up 200,000 additional 4G sites, rolling out 5G in high-traffic areas, and improving customer support. The Department of Telecommunications projects the state-owned operator will reach operational breakeven by FY29 and achieve 98% nationwide coverage.

articles.headline: Siguler Guff and investors seek exit from retail chain Baazar Kolkata
articles.summary: Private equity firm Siguler Guff and other investors are exploring a sale of their 51% stake in retail chain Baazar Kolkata, seeking a valuation of ₹4,000-5,000 crore. The retailer operates over 250 stores across West Bengal and 10 other states. O3 Capital is reportedly advising on the transaction as the company attracts interest from other private equity funds and strategic buyers.

articles.headline: Kharif crop sowing remains below last year despite monsoon revival
articles.summary: Farmers in India planted crops across 96.8 million hectares as of 7 August 2026, remaining 1.9% below previous year levels despite a recent intensification of monsoon rains. Rice acreage saw a significant drop of 1.6 million hectares compared to last year. While oilseed cultivation rose, pulses and coarse cereals trailed, with the government expecting further rains to boost planting.

articles.headline: Parliament passes bill to recognize digital bank records as legal evidence
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, replacing a 135-year-old law. The new legislation allows electronic and digital records maintained by banks to be recognized as admissible evidence in legal proceedings. The bill, previously passed by the Lok Sabha, modernizes the judicial process to align with paperless banking practices.

articles.headline: India considers restricting sugarcane use for ethanol to control sugar prices
articles.summary: The Indian government is considering limits on the amount of sugarcane diverted for ethanol production for the season starting in October. The move aims to boost domestic sugar output and stabilize record-high prices following reduced rainfall in major producing states like Maharashtra and Karnataka. Discussions involve balancing energy goals with food security and inflation control.

articles.headline: Trai mandates 1601-series numbers for service calls by non-banking entities
articles.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) has directed utilities, logistics, and other non-financial entities to use the 1601-series for service and transactional calls. The directive aims to distinguish legitimate service calls from promotional spam. Trai emphasized that these dedicated numbers must not be used for marketing purposes by any entity.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha passes bill to establish National Tribunals Commission
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, proposing a National Tribunals Commission to oversee quasi-judicial bodies. The commission, led by a former Supreme Court judge, will manage member appointments, monitor performance, and handle complaints. The reform aims to address persistent vacancies and case backlogs across 16 tribunals and appellate bodies.

articles.headline: New RBI loan recovery guidelines to take effect in January 2027
articles.summary: The RBI announced final loan recovery guidelines effective January 2027 to prevent borrower harassment. Banks must monitor recovery agencies, ensuring agents are certified and do not use harsh methods like abusive language, social media shaming, or excessive messaging. The move follows incidents like a 2022 death linked to recovery processes at Mahindra Finance.

articles.headline: Domestic institutional investors pump over 5 trillion into Indian equities
articles.summary: Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) including banks, insurers, and mutual funds have invested over ₹5 trillion in Indian shares so far in 2026. This marks the third consecutive year crossing this threshold, signaling strong confidence in the Indian economy. While foreign portfolio investors have been heavy sellers, recent trends suggest a potential reversal in interest.

articles.headline: Data centres emerge as preferred asset class for real estate investment
articles.summary: Data centres in India saw a significant increase in institutional real estate investment during the April-June 2026 period. They accounted for nearly 40% of total inflows, becoming the second-most preferred asset class after office spaces. This shift highlights the growing demand for digital infrastructure as institutional capital diversifies beyond traditional real estate.

articles.headline: Indian bank credit growth reaches 17 percent amid economic revival hopes
articles.summary: Non-food bank credit growth in India surpassed 17% for the fortnight ended 15 July 2026, the highest rate in two years. The growth is broad-based across agriculture, industry, services, and retail sectors. Increased industrial credit to large companies and a shift toward secured retail lending suggest the start of a durable credit cycle supported by rising private sector participation.

articles.headline: Lightstorm secures 2,500 crore debt for data centre network expansion
articles.summary: Network infrastructure firm Lightstorm secured a ₹2,500 crore long-term debt facility from IndusInd Bank. The capital will fund terrestrial and subsea fiber projects connecting Indian data centre clusters with hubs in Southeast Asia, Japan, and the US. The company aims to capitalize on India's growing digital data generation, which currently outpaces local storage capacity.

articles.headline: OpenAI halts work on Astra model due to cybersecurity risks
articles.summary: OpenAI has paused internal work on its upcoming Astra AI model after discovery that the system is highly proficient at cybersecurity tasks. The company stated that the model could potentially reach a "critical threshold" for identifying and developing zero-day exploits without human intervention. The pause allows for the implementation of stricter safety safeguards.

articles.headline: GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen considers withdrawing 56 billion dollar eBay bid
articles.summary: GameStop Corp. CEO Ryan Cohen is reportedly considering pulling a $56 billion offer for eBay Inc. Sources indicate Cohen may instead propose a partnership or joint venture to leverage GameStop's 1,600 retail locations. The potential deal aimed to increase market share in high-margin categories like collectibles and trading cards, but plans are now being reassessed.

articles.headline: Securities Appellate Tribunal case backlog reaches six-year high
articles.summary: Pending cases before the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) rose to 1,066 in FY26, the highest in six years. While fresh appeals have slowed, pendency is driven by a persistent shortage of judicial and technical members, limiting the number of benches available. Notable delays include the Wadia family’s appeal against Sebi orders, which took four years to resolve.

articles.headline: Global ammonia price drop provides relief to Indian fertilizer companies
articles.summary: Fertilizer stocks saw a lift as global ammonia prices retreated by approximately 20% from their peaks. Analysts suggest the price drop provides margin relief for non-urea fertilizer makers like Coromandel International and Paradeep Phosphates. However, benefits are partially offset by elevated sulphur costs and uncertainty surrounding conflict in West Asia.

articles.headline: US shifts to economic pressure over military strikes against Iran
articles.summary: President Donald Trump indicated a shift toward using economic pressure rather than fresh military strikes to subdue Iran. Trump noted that a naval blockade is deepening Iran's financial woes and high inflation. Meanwhile, Tehran continues to demand the lifting of sanctions and war reparations as conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to global energy shipping.

articles.headline: Raymond Realty expands Mumbai presence with major redevelopment projects
articles.summary: Raymond Realty Ltd is stepping up its expansion into Mumbai’s redevelopment market, signing two new projects in Parel and Kandivali with a combined value of ₹11,500 crore. The developer is shifting focus from its legacy land in Thane to asset-light joint development agreements. The strategy targets high demand for modernizing aging residential societies in land-scarce Mumbai.

articles.headline: Indian box office footfall rises 5 percent in first half of 2026
articles.summary: Cinema attendance in India reached 378 million in the first half of 2026, a 5% increase over the previous year. However, recovery is uneven, driven largely by a few major hits like "Dhurandhar: The Revenge." While Tier-II and Tier-III cities show consistent growth, metros remain selective. Industry experts hope a strong festive release slate will sustain the momentum.

articles.headline: Bombay High Court seeks government response on flavoured liquor prohibition
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court has asked the Centre to respond to a petition challenging the FSSAI's ban on flavoured rum and whisky. Alco-bev makers, including the producer of Old Monk, argued the prohibition is causing daily losses of ₹1 crore. The regulator had objected to added flavourings in spirits labeled as standardized, while makers claim the products have been safe for decades.

articles.headline: Air India pilot undergoes second drug test after mid-air turbulence incident
articles.summary: An Air India flight commander is undergoing a second round of drug screening following severe mid-air turbulence that injured passengers and crew. Initial tests prompted the need for confirmatory analysis to check for psychoactive substances. The Aircraft Accidents Investigation Bureau is leading the probe into the flight, which dropped 300 feet during the incident.

articles.headline: AstraZeneca Pharma India reports 32 percent decline in quarterly profit
articles.summary: AstraZeneca Pharma India Ltd reported a 32% drop in net profit to ₹37.93 crore for the June quarter. While revenue from operations grew to ₹682.79 crore, higher expenses significantly impacted the bottom line. The company's total expenses for the period rose to ₹641.03 crore, compared to ₹462.49 crore in the same quarter the previous year.

articles.headline: Hindustan Copper to sell ore from Chilean mines to Indian firms
articles.summary: State-run Hindustan Copper plans to sell copper concentrate from newly acquired Chilean mines to domestic firms like Hindalco and Adani. The company is in talks for a joint venture with Chile’s Codelco to mine and sell the metal to meet India’s growing demand. The initiative aims to secure raw material supplies as India increases its focus on copper-intensive industries.

articles.headline: Reliance Retail uses vast store network to scale JioMart delivery
articles.summary: JioMart is transforming Reliance Retail’s 3,100 stores into a digital distribution engine to compete in the quick-commerce market. Average daily orders crossed 2 million in the March quarter, surpassing Swiggy Instamart. Unlike competitors using dedicated dark stores, JioMart leverages its existing supermarkets and electronics outlets to fulfill hyperlocal orders across 1,200 cities.

articles.headline: Norton Motorcycles executive Nevijo Mance exits ahead of global expansion
articles.summary: Nevijo Mance, executive director at Norton Motorcycles, has stepped down for personal reasons as the TVS-owned brand prepares for international expansion. Mance was responsible for product design and engineering. His exit comes as Norton plans a phased rollout across the UK, Europe, India, and the US, targeting 20,000 annual units and 200 global dealer touchpoints.

articles.headline: India’s ultra-wealthy shift toward rare and eccentric luxury items
articles.summary: India's wealthiest consumers are increasingly moving away from recognizable logos toward rare, eccentric, and hard-to-source luxury products. High-demand items include Balenciaga "garbage bags," life-sized Ferrari show cars, and limited-edition collectibles. This shift reflects a desire for exclusivity and "quiet luxury" among India's growing population of ultra-high-net-worth individuals.

articles.headline: Google AI head Demis Hassabis moves to chief scientist role
articles.summary: Alphabet has announced a management shake-up where Demis Hassabis will transition from managing Google’s AI strategy to becoming the company’s chief scientist. The move follows concerns over Google’s execution in the AI race despite its scientific leads. Hassabis, who recently won a Nobel Prize, will focus on scientific breakthroughs while Koray Kavukcuoglu takes on expanded operational roles.

articles.headline: Gen Z embraces traditional analogue hobbies to combat digital overload
articles.summary: Younger teenagers and twenty-somethings are increasingly taking up "grandma hobbies" like knitting, crocheting, and pickling to seek relief from digital overstimulation. These tactile, slow-paced activities offer a creative outlet and a sense of autonomy away from academic and workplace pressures. Psychologists note that these hobbies help improve focus and provide an "analogue reset."

articles.headline: Mutual fund SIP closure ratio rises as investors react to volatility
articles.summary: Data shows a sharp rise in the closure of mutual fund systematic investment plans (SIPs) as investors react to short-term market volatility. The number of five-year-plus SIPs in direct plans shrank by 35% in FY26. Financial experts warn that quitting early disrupts compounding benefits and that staying invested through cycles significantly reduces the risk of negative returns.

articles.headline: Kharif sowing deficit narrows to less than 2% in August
articles.summary: The area under kharif crop sowing reached 88% of the season's normal area by August 7. Higher planting of nearly 74 lakh hectares during the first week of August helped narrow the year-on-year deficit. While oilseeds acreage has exceeded last year's levels, paddy and coarse cereals still report lower coverage. The South-West monsoon rainfall deficit currently stands at 12%.

articles.headline: Household savings shift to cash and deposits as equity flows decline
articles.summary: Indian households are moving towards safer, liquid assets, with bank deposits rising 22% to ₹15.3 lakh crore in FY26. Analysis of RBI data shows currency holdings doubled to ₹4.15 lakh crore, while direct equity flows turned negative with an outflow of ₹79,890 crore. Experts attribute this trend to market uncertainty and high interest rates, rather than a permanent structural shift.

articles.headline: UPI merchant fees worry mutual fund industry and distributors
articles.summary: The mutual fund industry is concerned that proposed Merchant Discount Rates (MDR) on UPI transactions could erode profit margins. With UPI accounting for nearly 45% of new Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs), distributors fear that additional costs may be passed on to investors or deter digital adoption in smaller cities. The government maintains that consumers will remain exempt from charges.

articles.headline: Demand for AI skills drives rebound in campus placement salaries
articles.summary: Engineering colleges report a shift towards higher compensation bands as companies prioritize AI and digital capabilities. Entry-level packages of ₹3-4 lakh are being replaced by offers in the ₹7-12 lakh range at tier-1 IT firms. Bulk hirers like TCS and Infosys plan to onboard 20,000-25,000 graduates each this year, focusing on roles involving automation and cloud technologies.

articles.headline: Mumbai start-up Techno Defence breaks Western monopoly on missile cooling
articles.summary: Techno Defence Pvt Ltd has developed an indigenous Joule-Thomson (JT) Cooler, a critical 10-gram device that cools missile infrared sensors to -196°C. Supported by DRDO's Technology Development Fund, the breakthrough ends the dominance of Western nations in this strategic technology. The success opens doors for high-value defence exports and enhances national missile precision capabilities.

articles.headline: Death toll reaches 47 after major earthquake in Cali, Colombia
articles.summary: A powerful earthquake struck the Choco region of Colombia, resulting in at least 47 deaths. The epicentre was located in San Jose Del Palmar, approximately 400 km west of Bogota. Residents and rescue teams are digging through the debris of collapsed buildings as authorities continue to assess the total damage in the community of 4,800 people.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland and Drivn partner for electric truck financing
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Drivn to provide comprehensive financial solutions for its electric vehicle customers. The partnership aims to make e-truck ownership more accessible through flexible financing, leasing, and fleet management options, supporting the adoption of sustainable commercial transport in India.

articles.headline: Zee Entertainment Q1 net profit nearly halves amid tax expenses
articles.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises reported a 48% drop in net profit to ₹74.3 crore for the June quarter, impacted by tax expenses for previous years and higher advertising spends. While subscription revenue grew 16% due to digital growth and linear pricing, domestic ad revenue continued to struggle. The company remains optimistic about sports content following the run-up to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

articles.headline: Bharat Forge reports Q1 loss due to German subsidiary restructuring
articles.summary: Pune-based Bharat Forge posted a consolidated net loss of ₹90 crore for Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of ₹284 crore last year. The loss was driven by restructuring provisions of ₹330 crore at its German subsidiary. Despite the loss, revenue grew 19% led by strong performance in defence and forgings. The board also approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 crore in capital.

articles.headline: ONGC and Shell sign pact for deepwater oil and gas exploration
articles.summary: ONGC and Shell Energy India have signed a non-binding MoU to explore joint opportunities in deepwater offshore blocks and liquefied natural gas sourcing. The collaboration involves potential farm-in arrangements and joint participation in future bidding rounds under India's Open Acreage Licensing Policy. The move aims to bring international expertise into India's samudra manthan initiative.

articles.headline: Ola Electric narrows net loss to ₹336 crore in June quarter
articles.summary: Ola Electric reported a narrower net loss of ₹336 crore for Q1 FY27, down from ₹428 crore a year earlier. The company benefited from the reversal of a ₹57 crore provision previously earmarked for PLI scheme penalties. However, revenue fell 45% year-on-year to ₹455 crore as volumes remained sluggish. The company expects operating expenses to decline further in coming quarters.

articles.headline: Iran demands US concessions before reopening Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Iran has stated that reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil waterway, depends on the US paying compensation for damages and lifting sanctions. While talks with Oman on new shipping lanes are progressing constructsively, Iranian officials listed ending US threats and removing a naval blockade as key conditions. About a fifth of the world's oil and LNG flows through the strait.

articles.headline: Nifty 50 could deliver 14-17% returns in FY27: Birla MF
articles.summary: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC expects the Nifty 50 to rebound with 14-17% returns in FY27, driven by a sharp revival in corporate earnings and consumption trends. The fund house noted that capital expenditure by India Inc is showing signs of revival, with top listed companies generating ₹19 lakh crore in profit in FY26. Valuations remain in an expensive zone despite recent corrections.

articles.headline: BSE to replace Wipro in Nifty 50 index from September 30
articles.summary: India's oldest stock exchange, BSE, will join the benchmark Nifty 50 index starting September 30, replacing IT giant Wipro. The change is part of the National Stock Exchange's half-yearly review. Wipro will move to the Nifty Next 50 index. Other changes include LIC and Meesho being added to the Nifty 200, while firms like Indian Hotels and United Spirits will exit the Nifty 100.

articles.headline: Paytm shares surge 10% after Bernstein raises target price
articles.summary: Shares of One97 Communications, Paytm's parent, hit a 52-week high after Bernstein raised its target price to ₹2,200. The brokerage cited potential revenue gains from the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions, which could add significant value to Paytm's EBITDA by FY28. Bernstein expects Paytm to capture 3-4 basis points of incremental payment margins.

articles.headline: Zee and Punit Goenka appeal to SAT against SEBI ban
articles.summary: Zee Entertainment and CEO Punit Goenka have moved the Securities Appellate Tribunal against a SEBI order barring them from the securities market. SEBI's probe relates to the alleged unauthorized use of Zee's property as security for loans taken by Essel Group entities. The appellants seek a stay on the ban to proceed with a ₹3,143 crore preferential issue of warrants to promoters.

articles.headline: Affluent consumption may moderate as hiring slows: BNP Paribas
articles.summary: A report by BNP Paribas warns that consumption by affluent Indian households—those earning over ₹10 lakh annually—may moderate due to subdued hiring in the IT and financial sectors. Wage growth has softened to around 7% from pandemic-era highs. While welfare schemes support rural income, the second half of the fiscal year could see slower growth in consumer staples and durables.

articles.headline: Government introduces MMDR Amendment Bill to regulate mining taxes
articles.summary: The government introduced the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill in the Lok Sabha to facilitate faster exploration of critical minerals. The Bill proposes that the Union government control the regulation of mineral-bearing lands and sets conditions on States' taxation of mineral rights. It aims to provide certainty and stability to the national mining sector.

articles.headline: US increases H1-B and L-1 visa extension fees
articles.summary: The US has published new rules requiring large employers with over 50 staff to pay an additional fee of $4,000 for H1-B and $4,500 for L-1 visa extensions. Effective September 9, the 9-11 response fee, which previously only applied to initial petitions, will now hit routine extension requests. Major Indian IT firms relying on the onshore-offshore model will face higher sponsorship costs.

articles.headline: GeM portal posts sharp rise in GMV to ₹1.55 lakh crore
articles.summary: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has recorded a surge in gross merchandise value to over ₹1.55 lakh crore, according to Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal. Launched in 2016, the platform now hosts over 12.28 lakh MSEs and 42,000 start-ups. The Minister noted that GeM is driving self-reliance and strengthening accountability through end-to-end digital procurement for government departments.

articles.headline: HDFC Bank cuts marginal cost of lending rate by 5 bps
articles.summary: HDFC Bank has reduced its marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) by 5 basis points across key tenures, effective August 7. The one-year MCLR now stands at 8.4%. Analysts attribute the cut to easing deposit costs and strong inflows into foreign currency non-resident (FCNR) deposits. This move contrasts with Bank of India, which recently raised its one-year MCLR to 8.8%.

articles.headline: Proposed Tribunal Commission may template future judicial appointments
articles.summary: The government indicated that the institutional architecture of the new National Tribunals Commission could serve as a model for reforming the selection of judges to higher courts. The proposed commission gives the judiciary a decisive voice while introducing a permanent secretariat and recorded assessment parameters. This approach aims to address criticisms of the existing collegium system.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu announces bonus payments for paddy and sugarcane
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay announced a special incentive of ₹289 per quintal for fine variety paddy and a ₹709.50 per tonne bonus for sugarcane. Sugarcane farmers will now receive ₹4,000 per tonne, marking the highest single-year increase in state incentives. The measures are intended to support rural livelihoods ahead of the procurement season starting September 1.

articles.headline: Southern States account for 80% of India's gold loan portfolio
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, and Kerala together hold over 80% of the gold loans outstanding in India's public sector banks. As of March 2026, the total gold loan outstanding was over ₹11.31 lakh crore. Tamil Nadu leads with ₹4 lakh crore. Despite the rapid credit growth, gross NPA ratios for gold loans have declined to 0.12%, reflecting stable asset quality.

articles.headline: CAG report highlights connectivity issues at Bangalore Metro
articles.summary: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) found that Bangalore Metro failed to achieve its projected ridership due to poor integration with other transport modes. The audit noted a lack of last-mile connectivity and inadequate parking facilities. Daily footfalls in BMTC buses also reduced significantly, indicating that the metro has not yet drawn enough private vehicle users.

articles.headline: Supreme Court permits TMC's Abhishek Banerjee to travel for treatment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has allowed Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee to travel abroad for three weeks to receive eye treatment. The court emphasized that every individual has the right to choose their medical assistance. The ruling came despite objections from the West Bengal government, which cited pending criminal cases and argued that adequate facilities exist within India.

articles.headline: French agency BEA to assist in Air India altitude loss probe
articles.summary: France’s Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety is collaborating with India's AAIB to investigate a serious incident involving an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight. The aircraft experienced a sudden 300-foot altitude loss during cruise on August 4. Investigators are examining multiple momentary technical snags reported by the crew. Both pilots have been grounded pending the probe.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Congo set to rise as health search expands
articles.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is expected to worsen as health officials move toward door-to-door case finding. Deaths have doubled in less than three weeks, with a case-fatality ratio of 45.5%. The WHO and Africa CDC are shifting strategy because 60-70% of victims are currently dying at home rather than in treatment centers, risking wider community transmission.

articles.headline: Over 100 killed as 7.4 magnitude earthquake strikes Colombia
articles.summary: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake hit Colombia, centered near San Jose Del Palmar, killing at least 111 people and injuring 87 others. Hundreds of buildings collapsed, leaving residents trapped under debris. President Abelardo de la Espriella declared an emergency to expedite recovery funding as rescue workers continue searching for survivors in cities like Cali and Pereira.

articles.headline: Rights groups call for overhaul in Aravalis high-powered committee hearings
articles.summary: Civil rights groups in Rajasthan have demanded an overhaul of the Supreme Court-appointed committee's hearing process on the Aravali hill range. Activists allege the current process lacks inclusive public participation and that the mining lobby dominated recent sessions. The panel is tasked with reviewing the delineation of the hills and their ecological impact before August 31.

articles.headline: CAG report flags declining infrastructure investment in Delhi under AAP government
articles.summary: A Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report tabled in the Delhi Assembly noted a declining trend in capital expenditure between 2015 and 2025. Subsidies rose by 172.48%, primarily due to electricity costs, leaving limited fiscal space for long-term assets. The report observed that capital expenditure ranged from 7% to 15% of total spending, reflecting constraints in infrastructure growth.

articles.headline: Delhi CM defends three-child limit for Lakshmi Yojana aid beneficiaries
articles.summary: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta defended the three-child cap for the government's Lakshmi Yojana, which provides ₹2,500 monthly to women. Responding to criticism from Arvind Kejriwal, the CM stated the condition is intended to protect women's health. She emphasized that family planning decisions remain personal but the government prioritizes the well-being of mothers over population expansion.

articles.headline: Over 800 principal and vice-principal posts vacant in Delhi government schools
articles.summary: According to a UPSC recruitment advertisement, 828 principal and vice-principal positions are vacant in Delhi government schools. The vacancies include 124 principal and 704 vice-principal roles across approximately 1,090 schools. The Directorate of Education currently operates with 50% of these senior administrative posts earmarked for direct recruitment to fill the gap.

articles.headline: High Court gives Arvind Kejriwal four weeks to respond to ED
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court granted former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal four weeks to respond to Enforcement Directorate pleas challenging his acquittal in two cases. The ED alleges Mr. Kejriwal intentionally avoided summonses related to the excise policy investigation. A trial court previously held that the agency failed to prove intentional disobedience by the AAP leader.

articles.headline: Delhi Police maps 2,500 homeless children in city safety campaign
articles.summary: The Special Police Unit for Women and Children mapped 2,500 homeless children found begging at major intersections during July. The initiative, part of the 'Child Beggar-Free Delhi' campaign, recorded the children's coordinates and photographs to assist social welfare departments. The effort aims to reduce the vulnerability of these children to crimes such as drug trafficking and theft.

articles.headline: Gurugram woman arrested for domestic help assault; released on bail
articles.summary: A 52-year-old woman was arrested in Gurugram for allegedly assaulting her domestic help at an apartment in Sector 42. A viral video showed the accused hitting the victim and pulling her hair after a work-related argument. The woman was booked for voluntarily causing hurt and wrongful confinement before being released on bail. The victim had resigned shortly after the incident.

articles.headline: Sanitation worker dies while cleaning manhole without safety gear in Faridabad
articles.summary: A 34-year-old sanitation worker died and another was critically injured while cleaning a manhole outside a factory in Faridabad's Sector 25. The victims entered the sewer without safety equipment and suffocated due to toxic fumes. Police have initiated an investigation following allegations of negligence by the factory owner. Bunty, 37, remains under medical treatment.

articles.headline: Centre gives in-principle nod to ₹2,574 crore Wazirabad water supply project
articles.summary: A Union Finance Ministry committee granted 'in-principle' approval for the ₹2,574 crore Wazirabad Water Supply Improvement Project, assisted by the Asian Development Bank. The project involves upgrading water treatment plants, replacing damaged pipelines, and expanding the distribution network. The initiative aims to provide reliable water access to Delhi's growing population.

articles.headline: JNU students hold outdoor discussion on Umar Khalid's book despite ban
articles.summary: After JNU administration cancelled permission for an auditorium event, the students' union held an outdoor discussion on a book by former student Umar Khalid. The talk focused on 'Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories'. Members of ABVP protested the event, chanting slogans against Khalid, who has been in jail for nearly six years awaiting trial for the 2020 Delhi riots case.

articles.headline: Manipur government and United Naga Council hold 'fruitful' first round talks
articles.summary: Talks between the Manipur government and the United Naga Council (UNC) were described as a 'fruitful icebreaker' following highway blockades. The UNC is demanding the abrogation of the Suspension of Operations pact with Kuki groups and action against those involved in killing Naga civilians. Both sides agreed to continue discussions, though the UNC maintains its blockade for now.

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks reply on issuance of identity cards for NRC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court sought responses from the Centre and Assam government regarding the delay in issuing National Identity Cards to those included in the 2019 NRC list. Petitions stated that the process is at a standstill for over 3.11 crore included persons. Meanwhile, former NRC coordinator Hitesh Dev Sarma has sought a re-verification of the list, citing multiple inaccuracies.

articles.headline: Suvendu Adhikari admits police negligence in custodial death of TMC worker
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited the family of TMC worker Birju Keot, who died in police custody at Halisahar. Adhikari announced ₹10 lakh compensation and a job for the victim's wife, admitting that police negligence was evident. An investigating officer has been suspended and a magistrate-level probe ordered. Adhikari also faced sloganeering during his visit.

articles.headline: Punjab Assembly passes nine Bills in one day amid Opposition walkout
articles.summary: The Punjab Assembly passed nine Bills, including those on university establishment and tree protection, in a single day. Opposition parties slammed the move as 'majoritarian arrogance', claiming they were given insufficient time to study the legislations. The passed Bills cover diverse sectors such as education, taxation, and the regulation of fees in un-aided educational institutions.

articles.headline: Meghalaya’s Garo Hills council bars non-tribals from voting or contesting polls
articles.summary: The Garo Hills Autonomous District Council approved amendments to election rules that will bar non-tribals from voting or contesting in council elections. The move establishes a separate electoral roll for the Sixth Schedule body, replacing the use of the general Assembly roll. The amendment follows long-standing demands to protect the rights and interests of the Garo tribal people.

articles.headline: Retired health official arrested for running female foeticide ring in Maharashtra
articles.summary: Dr. Chandrakant Gunda Gaikwad, a former district civil surgeon, was arrested in Kolhapur for allegedly orchestrating a massive female foeticide racket. Gaikwad reportedly admitted to performing up to 250 illegal abortions. The State government announced plans to invoke the MCOCA against such networks. The case highlights deep-rooted son preference and the failure of existing safeguards.

articles.headline: Moradabad driver dies after alleged assault by kanwariyas following road accident
articles.summary: A 24-year-old driver died in a hospital days after being allegedly assaulted by a group of kanwariyas in Hapur, Uttar Pradesh. The assault occurred following a collision between the victim's goods vehicle and an autorickshaw carrying the pilgrims. Cross-FIRs have been filed, with the autorickshaw driver's family also alleging that the victim used his vehicle as a weapon.

articles.headline: Prosecution under PMLA after predicate offence conviction is not double jeopardy
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court ruled that prosecuting a person under the PMLA after they have been convicted of a predicate offence does not constitute a second trial for the same crime. The court dismissed petitions from 11 individuals convicted in a notes exchange scam, stating that money laundering is an independent statutory offence distinct from the original criminal act.

articles.headline: Karnataka has second-highest number of EV charging stations in India
articles.summary: Ministry of Heavy Industries data reveals Karnataka has 6,805 electric vehicle charging stations, the second-highest in the country after Maharashtra. The State accounts for nearly 13% of India's total 52,718 stations. Experts attribute this growth to Karnataka's proactive 2017 EV policy, though they call for better standardization of tariffs and real-time availability data.

articles.headline: Google rolls back AI satellite image feature over deepfake safety concerns
articles.summary: Google withdrew an AI image-generation feature from Google Earth just one day after its launch due to misuse. Users bypass safeguards to create 'satellite deepfakes' depicting violence, terrorist attacks, and environmental disasters. Experts warned that fake satellite imagery could be used for misinformation in conflicts or real estate scams, highlighting flaws in AI guardrails.

articles.headline: High-level panel visits Jammu to study demographic changes in border areas
articles.summary: A four-member committee led by former IAS and IPS officers arrived in Jammu to study demographic shifts in regions bordering Pakistan. The team will visit Hiranagar, where 450 Rohingyas are detained, and meet civil society groups. The study, mandated by the Union Home Ministry, focuses on settlement patterns and their impact on national security in Kathua and Samba districts.

articles.headline: RTI replies confirm at least ten people injured by pellets on July 20
articles.summary: Hospital records obtained through RTI show that at least 10 people suffered pellet gun injuries during the July 20 protest in Delhi. Lady Hardinge Medical College reported nine victims, while Safdarjung Hospital recorded one. The data contradicts initial denials regarding the use of such weapons. Among the injured were students, an artist, and a journalist.

articles.headline: Allahabad High Court upholds religious conversion of two Hindu women to Islam
articles.summary: The Allahabad High Court directed the release of two adult sisters who voluntarily converted to Islam, ruling that their father had unlawfully confined them. The court awarded ₹25 lakh compensation for the violation of their fundamental rights. The sisters, aged 35 and 20, are now free to reside and practice their faith of choice without state or parental interference.

articles.headline: Government adds 11 new entry points for international e-visa holders
articles.summary: The Union Home Ministry notified 11 new international entry points for e-visa holders, including airports in Bhopal and Tirupati and nine land ports. The expansion brings the total number of authorized ports to 88. The move is aimed at boosting tourism and facilitating easier travel for foreign nationals using the electronic visa regime for entry into India.

articles.headline: Russia's share in India's oil imports jumps to 48% in June
articles.summary: Russia's share of India's crude oil imports reached a record high of 48% in June 2026, despite threats of U.S. sanctions. India imported 8.7 million metric tonnes of Russian oil, a 25% increase from the previous year. Simultaneously, imports from the UAE rose to historic levels. Combined, Russia and the UAE now account for nearly two-thirds of India's total oil imports.

articles.headline: Mojtaba Khamenei rejigs Iran’s top leadership; Mohsen Rezaei to head security
articles.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointed former Guards commander Mohsen Rezaei as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. The leadership reshuffle also saw Ali Abdollahi named as head of the armed forces. The changes in Iran's top security and military establishments come amid heightened regional tensions and ongoing disputes with the United States.

articles.headline: Taiwan tests internet throttling for first time during annual war exercises
articles.summary: Taiwan slowed mobile internet access in a large part of the island during its annual Han Kuang war games to simulate communication disruptions. The 'throttling' drill, conducted in Taichung, restricted users to basic services for 30 minutes. The exercise aims to prepare the nation for potential infrastructure attacks or natural disasters amid ongoing threats from China.

articles.headline: India clinches 17 medals at u-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championships
articles.summary: Indian fencers won 17 medals, including four gold, on the opening day of the under-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championships in Lagos, Nigeria. Gold medalists included Nikhil Wagh in men's sabre, Joys Ashita in women's foil, Prachi Lohan in women's epee, and Jeferlin in women's sabre. The team reached the podium in all six individual events across Sabre, Foil, and Epee categories.

articles.headline: Scientists turn to sharks for hurricane predictions along U.S. East Coast
articles.summary: University of Delaware researchers are using sharks equipped with electronic tags to measure ocean temperature, salinity, and depth. This data helps scientists predict hurricane intensity by monitoring the ocean's 'mixed layer' heat. Sharks are ideal observers because they surface often, allowing tags to transmit real-time data to satellites as they swim across the Atlantic.

articles.headline: IPOs Flood Indian Market with 34 Issues Expected by September
articles.summary: Around 34 companies are racing to launch initial public offerings (IPOs) before the September 30 deadline. These companies seek to raise approximately ₹45,000 crore, aiming to utilize the current market window before renewed regulatory approvals are required.

articles.headline: Lawmakers Support Restrictions on Social Media for Minors
articles.summary: Members of Parliament from various political parties have proposed private members' bills to limit social media access for minors. The proposed Safeguarding Healthy Internet Environment for Little Digital-Natives (SHIELD) Bill includes features like parental dashboards and night-time curfews.

articles.headline: Digital Spending via UPI and Cards Surpasses Cash Payments
articles.summary: Retail digital payments via UPI and cards have overtaken cash withdrawals and debit card usage in India. UPI transactions grew 16.9% year-on-year, while cash withdrawals at ATMs fell 6.8%, signaling a major shift in consumer payment behavior.

articles.headline: Corporate Revenues Rise but Profits Fall Amid High Costs
articles.summary: Indian corporate earnings for the June quarter show revenue growth of 7% but a 25.1% drop in net profits. The decline is attributed to rising interest margins and high raw material costs across sectors like auto and consumer goods.

articles.headline: Centre Proposes Mining Law Changes to Curtail State Taxing Powers
articles.summary: The Union government has proposed changes to mining laws to limit the powers of state governments to impose taxes or cesses on mineral rights. The move aims to prevent excessive fiscal burdens that make mining operations unviable following a Supreme Court verdict.

articles.headline: TCS Reports Possible Exposure of Employee Data via Cyber Incident
articles.summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported a potential data breach involving the exposure of some employee-related information. The company stated that no customer data or core systems were affected, and the incident occurred through a phishing attack on an employee.

articles.headline: Delhi Airport Operator to Raise ₹3,550 Crore via Bonds
articles.summary: Delhi International Airport Ltd (DIAL) plans to raise ₹3,550 crore through a 10-year bond issue. The proceeds will be used to refinance existing dollar-denominated notes of $522.6 million due for maturity in early 2027.

articles.headline: Sun Pharma Recalls Eye Drops After Bacterial Contamination Alert
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries has recalled its Predmet eye drops after a safety alert from the All India Ophthalmological Society. The recall follows reports of potential bacterial contamination in certain batches, which could lead to severe eye infections.

articles.headline: Purvah Green Power to Acquire 1.4 GW Solar Assets
articles.summary: Purvah Green Power, a subsidiary of CESC, has entered into an agreement to acquire 1.4 gigawatt-peak (GWp) of solar assets from ReNew. The deal, valued at an enterprise price of ₹4,859 crore, aims to bolster Purvah's renewable energy portfolio to 10 GW by 2032.

articles.headline: Quick Commerce Firms to Create 100,000 Temporary Jobs for Festive Season
articles.summary: Quick commerce and e-commerce firms in India are expected to hire over 100,000 temporary workers for the upcoming festive season. This represents a 35-40% increase compared to last year, driven by higher demand for fast deliveries and expanded logistics networks.

articles.headline: Banks Seek RBI Permission to Spread Mark-to-Market Losses
articles.summary: Indian lenders have requested the Reserve Bank of India for permission to spread their mark-to-market (MTM) losses over several quarters. The request comes as rising bond yields have impacted the valuation of banks' investment portfolios.

articles.headline: Bhagwati Products Delays IPO Amid Volatile Chip Prices
articles.summary: Bhagwati Products, a joint venture between Micromax and China's Huaqin Technology, has deferred its proposed ₹2,000-₹5,000 crore IPO by two to three quarters. The delay is attributed to volatility in chip prices and a slump in the smartphone market.

articles.headline: Aviation Ministry Evaluates Request for Airport Cross-Holding Waiver
articles.summary: The Union aviation ministry is reviewing a request to waive the cross-holding cap for private airport operators. The current rule limits a company from holding stakes in multiple major airports, but proponents argue a waiver would encourage investment and competition.

articles.headline: Opposition Rejects Government Proposal for Home Minister's Statement
articles.summary: Opposition parties have rejected the government's offer for a statement by the Home Minister on student protests, demanding instead a full-fledged debate and accountability for recent police actions. The impasse continues to disrupt parliamentary sessions.

articles.headline: Parliamentary Panel Criticizes Continued Suspension of National Talent Search Exam
articles.summary: A parliamentary standing committee has expressed concern over the suspension of the National Talent Search Examination (NTSE) since 2021. The panel termed the delay a "severe blow" to identifying and nurturing young talent across the country and urged immediate resumption.

articles.headline: Students Protest in Ranchi Demanding Examination and Recruitment Reforms
articles.summary: Hundreds of students in Ranchi marched towards the Jharkhand Assembly to protest against irregularities in state recruitment exams. Police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse the crowd, resulting in several injuries among both students and security personnel.

articles.headline: Panel Highlights Poor Execution of Free Coaching for Underprivileged Students
articles.summary: A parliamentary committee noted significant deficiencies in the implementation of the free coaching scheme for SC and OBC students. The panel observed that financial targets were not met and many eligible students were unable to access the benefits due to administrative hurdles.

articles.headline: NCP Faction Demands Bharat Ratna for Social Reformers
articles.summary: MPs from the Sharad Pawar-led NCP met Prime Minister Modi to request the Bharat Ratna for social reformers Mahatma Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, and Annabhau Sathe. They also raised issues concerning reservation and drought relief in Maharashtra.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Expresses Alarm Over Rising Drug Abuse in India
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has expressed serious concern over the increasing cases of drug abuse and trafficking across India. The court has directed the central and state governments to submit detailed reports on the measures being taken to curb the menace and improve rehabilitation.

articles.headline: Indian Envoys Hold Key Meetings with Nepal and Bangladesh Leaders
articles.summary: India's ambassadors to Nepal and Bangladesh held high-level meetings with the respective Prime Ministers to discuss bilateral ties and regional security. The discussions focused on infrastructure projects, trade cooperation, and stability in the neighborhood.

articles.headline: Food Safety Officials Seize Unsafe Food from Bengaluru Luxury Hotels
articles.summary: The Karnataka Food Safety and Standards Department conducted raids on 60 star hotels in Bengaluru, seizing over 1,000 kg of unsafe and misbranded food. Violations included the use of expired ingredients, lack of proper labeling, and unhygienic storage conditions.

articles.headline: Security Concerns Over Potential Crime Networks in Colombo Port City
articles.summary: Security agencies have raised alarms regarding the potential for transnational criminal networks to exploit the Colombo Port City project. Concerns include money laundering, cybercrime, and the use of the special economic zone as a hub for illicit activities.

articles.headline: Kannada Organizations Call for State Bandh Over Mekedatu Project
articles.summary: Several Kannada organizations have called for a statewide bandh on Thursday to protest against the delay in the Mekedatu drinking water project. The activists are demanding that the Karnataka government expedite the project despite opposition from Tamil Nadu.

articles.headline: Karnataka Council Session Likely to Face Political Turmoil
articles.summary: The upcoming session of the Karnataka Legislative Council is expected to be stormy, with the ruling Congress and opposition BJP-JD(S) alliance set for a confrontation over various issues, including the Mekedatu project and administrative lapses.

articles.headline: Indian Companies Adopt Hybrid AI Strategy to Balance Performance and Cost
articles.summary: Major Indian firms are increasingly adopting a hybrid AI approach, combining open-source and proprietary models. This strategy aims to optimize costs, enhance data security, and tailor AI applications to specific business needs while avoiding vendor lock-in.

articles.headline: Microsoft Expected to Unveil New Custom AI Chip in September
articles.summary: Microsoft is reportedly planning to launch its next-generation custom AI chip, Maia 300, in September. The move is part of the company's efforts to reduce its reliance on Nvidia and optimize its AI infrastructure for internal workloads and Azure customers.

articles.headline: Chinese AI Models Spark Global Price War with Low-Cost Offerings
articles.summary: The emergence of low-cost, high-performance AI models from Chinese labs is triggering a price war in the global AI market. US-based labs are facing pressure to lower their API pricing to remain competitive against efficient models like DeepSeek and Qwen.

articles.headline: Rapid Lifecycle of Frontier AI Models Challenges Enterprises
articles.summary: The rapid release cycle of new AI models is forcing companies to frequently update their infrastructure. Many frontier models are being replaced or retired within months, creating a need for flexible AI strategies that can adapt to the evolving technological landscape.

articles.headline: Volunteer Communities Drive AI Adoption at Grassroots Level in India
articles.summary: Volunteer-driven communities and 'AI evangelists' are organizing meetups and workshops in cities across India to promote the use of frontier AI tools. These grassroots efforts aim to bridge the gap between complex AI technology and practical applications for developers and startups.

articles.headline: Improved Rainfall Helps Narrow Gap in Kharif Crop Sowing Acreage
articles.summary: The gap in kharif crop sowing has narrowed as monsoon rains have improved across several parts of India. Data from the agriculture ministry shows that sowing of key crops like rice and pulses is nearing normal levels, boosting hopes for a good harvest.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Launches Campaign to Attract Investors from Tamil Nadu
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government is organizing roadshows in major cities of Tamil Nadu to attract investment in sectors like textiles and manufacturing. The initiative aims to highlight the state's competitive advantages and ease of doing business.

articles.headline: India Urged to Increase Rice Usage for Ethanol Production
articles.summary: A government report has suggested that India should increase its reliance on rice as a feedstock for ethanol production. The move aims to meet blending targets and reduce the dependence on sugar-based ethanol, which has faced supply constraints.

articles.headline: India's Digital Infrastructure Faces Risks from Post-Quantum Security Gaps
articles.summary: Experts have warned that India's digital infrastructure, including Aadhaar and banking systems, could be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks. The report highlights the need for a rapid transition to post-quantum cryptographic standards to safeguard national data.

articles.headline: Indian VCs Adjust Investment Strategies Amid High AI Stakes
articles.summary: Indian venture capital firms are modifying their investment strategies to focus more on AI startups. VCs are increasing their ticket sizes and conducting deeper technical due diligence to identify high-potential AI ventures in a competitive global market.

articles.headline: Info Edge Reports 43% Profit Growth Driven by Naukri and 99acres
articles.summary: Info Edge reported a 43% increase in its June quarter profit, supported by strong performance in its core recruitment portal Naukri.com and real estate platform 99acres. The company saw robust growth in billings and operational efficiency across its business segments.

articles.headline: South Korea Announces $3.5 Billion Fund to Boost Semiconductor Industry
articles.summary: The South Korean government has announced a $3.5 billion fund to support its domestic semiconductor industry. The initiative aims to provide low-interest loans and subsidies to chipmakers to maintain the country's global leadership in the memory chip market.

articles.headline: Meta Faces New Trial Over Child Safety and Mental Health Concerns
articles.summary: Meta is set to face a major trial in the US over allegations that its platforms, Instagram and Facebook, have negatively impacted the mental health of children. The trial will focus on the company's internal research and its failure to implement adequate safety measures.

articles.headline: EV Rental Startups Yulu and Bounce Seek Fresh Funding
articles.summary: Electric vehicle rental startups Yulu and Bounce are in talks to raise fresh capital to expand their fleets. The demand for gig-economy EV rentals is surging, driven by the growth of food and grocery delivery platforms in major Indian cities.

articles.headline: AI Hardware Startup Discovered Materials Raises $9 Million in Funding
articles.summary: Discovered Materials, a startup focused on developing new materials for AI chips, has raised $9 million in its latest funding round. The company aims to create more energy-efficient chips that can handle the high thermal loads of modern AI processing.

articles.headline: Space-Tech Startup GalaxEye Acquires Bengaluru-Based StarOps
articles.summary: Space-tech startup GalaxEye has acquired StarOps, a Bengaluru-based engineering firm, to strengthen its in-house satellite development capabilities. The acquisition will help GalaxEye accelerate its plans to launch a constellation of multi-sensor satellites.

articles.headline: Satellite Internet Adoption Remains Low Globally Despite Technological Advancements
articles.summary: A recent report indicates that satellite internet adoption remains limited to a small niche globally. High costs, latency issues, and the availability of terrestrial fiber connections have restricted its growth, despite the launch of several low-earth orbit satellite constellations.

articles.headline: Indian Super League Faces Crisis Following Tata Steel's Exit
articles.summary: The Indian Super League (ISL) is facing a significant challenge after Tata Steel announced the withdrawal of its team, Jamshedpur FC. The move has raised concerns about the league's commercial viability and the long-term commitment of corporate sponsors to Indian football.

articles.headline: FIFA President Infantino Faces Criticism from Continental Football Confederations
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino is facing backlash from the heads of several continental football confederations over his proposed changes to the international match calendar. The critics argue that the plans prioritize commercial gains over player welfare and the integrity of regional competitions.

articles.headline: Zostel Withdraws Legal Plea Against Oyo's Parent Company in Long-Running Dispute
articles.summary: Zostel has withdrawn its latest legal application against Oyo's parent company, PRISM, in the Delhi High Court. The move marks a pause in the long-standing legal battle between the two hospitality startups over acquisition and intellectual property issues.

articles.headline: Russian Sports Federations File New Appeals Against Global Bans
articles.summary: Several Russian sports federations have filed fresh appeals at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against their ongoing exclusion from international competitions. The federations argue that the bans are politically motivated and discriminatory against Russian athletes.

articles.headline: Trust Remains Paramount in Financial Services Despite Technological Advancements
articles.summary: Industry leaders at a recent forum emphasized that while technology like AI is transforming financial services, customer trust remains the most critical factor. They argued that tech should be used to enhance transparency and security rather than replace human judgment in high-stakes decisions.

articles.headline: Indian Corporate Sector Sees Revenue Growth but Lower Profits
articles.summary: Data from the June quarter shows that while Indian companies recorded a 7.2% increase in revenue, their combined net profit fell by 25.1%. The results reflect the impact of higher input costs and interest rates across key industrial sectors.

articles.headline: Market Experts Predict Indian Equities to Reach Record Highs in 2027
articles.summary: Market analysts suggest that Indian equity indices could reach new record highs by early 2027. The positive outlook is driven by expectations of steady economic growth, moderate inflation, and continued foreign institutional investment inflows.

articles.headline: India's Transition to Cashless Economy Accelerates with Rising Digital Payments
articles.summary: New data reveals that digital payments via UPI and cards have significantly surpassed cash-based transactions in India. The shift is particularly evident in retail and e-commerce segments, where consumers are increasingly opting for digital wallets and contactless payments.

articles.headline: Non-Banking Financial Companies Outperform Banks in Retail Lending Segment
articles.summary: Retail-focused NBFCs are growing faster than traditional banks in the retail loan segment. While credit card usage has slowed, NBFCs have seen a surge in demand for personal and consumer durable loans, particularly in smaller cities.

articles.headline: Dairy Firm Milky Mist Prepares for Initial Public Offering
articles.summary: Dairy product manufacturer Milky Mist is preparing for its initial public offering to fund its expansion plans. The company, known for its premium dairy products in South India, aims to use the proceeds to upgrade its manufacturing facilities and enter new markets.

articles.headline: Implementation of Microfinance Credit Guarantee Scheme Faces Challenges
articles.summary: The government's microfinance credit guarantee scheme has reportedly struggled to achieve its intended targets. Lenders have expressed concerns over the scheme's complex requirements and the slow pace of fund disbursement to small-scale borrowers.

articles.headline: Proposed Mining Bill Aims to Limit State Taxation Powers
articles.summary: A new central bill proposes to limit the powers of state governments to levy additional taxes on mining activities. The move aims to create a more uniform and predictable tax regime for the mining industry across India, following recent legal disputes over state-level cesses.

articles.headline: Iran Expresses Readiness to Engage in Negotiations with US
articles.summary: An Iranian government spokesperson stated that the country is prepared to enter into negotiations with the United States if certain conditions are met. The statement comes amid rising regional tensions and ongoing international efforts to revive the nuclear deal.

articles.headline: Intel to Sell $15 Billion Stake to Fund Expansion Plans
articles.summary: Intel Corp. plans to raise $15 billion through a share sale following a recent rally in its stock price. The funds will be used to support the company's ambitious plan to expand its chip manufacturing capacity and regain its leadership in the global semiconductor market.

articles.headline: Powerful Earthquake in Colombia Leaves Over 20 People Dead
articles.summary: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake in western Colombia has killed at least 20 people and injured dozens more. The quake caused widespread damage to buildings and infrastructure, leading to large-scale rescue and relief operations in the affected regions.

articles.headline: Sony and TSMC Discuss $6.4 Billion Joint Venture for Sensors
articles.summary: Sony and TSMC are reportedly in advanced talks to establish a $6.4 billion joint venture for a semiconductor sensor factory in Japan. The project aims to secure a stable supply of advanced image sensors for the global smartphone and automotive markets.

articles.headline: Anthropic and Partners to Build AI-Focused Data Centres Globally
articles.summary: AI startup Anthropic has partnered with Macquarie and GIC to develop a series of specialized data centres for AI workloads. The venture aims to build energy-efficient infrastructure that can handle the massive computing requirements of large language models.

articles.headline: Fashion Giant Shein Receives $25 Billion Valuation Ahead of Public Offering
articles.summary: Fast-fashion retailer Shein has reportedly been valued at around $22-25 billion as it prepares for its much-anticipated initial public offering. The valuation reflects the company's rapid global growth and its dominant position in the online fashion market.

articles.headline: Taiwan Conducts First Internet-Slowing Drills to Test Cyber Resilience
articles.summary: Taiwan has conducted its first-ever military drills that involve intentionally slowing down internet speeds to simulate a cyberattack. The exercise aims to test the resilience of the island's digital infrastructure and prepare for potential disruptions during a conflict.

articles.headline: US Announces New Fees for H1-B and L-1 Visa Extensions
